title: Avoid eagerly loading StoredFieldsReader in fetch phase

timeline.message:
Avoid eagerly loading StoredFieldsReader in fetch phase

Every time we create a hit document, we create a new SourceLookup and call
setSegmentAndDocument. This in turn creates a new StoredFieldsReader, which is
pretty expensive. In scenarios where you are retrieving a lot of hits, this can
add significant overhead. Prior to version 7.11, we did not create a new
SourceLookup per hit, so this is a performance regression.

This PR updates setSegmentAndDocument to avoid eagerly creating a
new StoredFieldsReader (through StoredFieldsReader#getMergeInstance).
timeline.author: Julie Tibshirani

timeline.body: Hi @jtibshirani, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

Some notes:
* An alternative would be to introduce `SourceLookup#setDoc`, which sets the document without the leaf reader context. This felt less solid, and I wanted to avoid touching the `HitContext` -- source handling in the fetch phase is very complex and doesn't have strong test coverage!
* This gives more motivation for adding fetch benchmarks ([rally-tracks#199](https://github.com/elastic/rally-tracks/issues/199)). I'm also guessing that EQL tests might have caught it, which didn't exist back in 7.11.
I restored this class, which was only very recently deleted because it was unused.

timeline.body: The main issue is that `getSequentialStoredFieldsReader` calls `StoredFieldsReader#getMergeInstance`, which creates a new stored fields reader. I wonder if this could be optimized in Lucene to avoid recreating it every time 🤔

reply.body: I think ideally we'd like to push as much of this up into Lucene as possible, as it is all hacks at the moment and if anything changes in how stored fields are merged then we are in trouble.
